title: the masks come off
hookLine: the year ends the way it began, with dice, and then the five servants of Virata's court take the royal seats
carry: acharya devo bhava: the teacher's trust is sacred
last: A PRINCE RUNS, A TEACHER FOLLOWS.

lines: THE LAST DAY OF THE MASKS.
cards: A conch sounds across the field, and the Kuru warriors know that sound. Arjuna is back.
He fights the whole raiding army with Uttara at the reins, and in the end uses a weapon that makes the Kuru warriors fall into a stupor.
He sends Uttara among them to take their fine upper cloths, for the princesses' dolls, as promised. The cattle go home. So does a prince who ran away that morning.
On this last day of the Virata story, the masks come off.

teach.b: Back at the palace, King Virata is overjoyed. My son has beaten the Kurus! He sits down to dice with Kanka and keeps praising Uttara.
Kanka says quietly: with Brihannala driving, how could he lose? Virata, angry, throws the dice in Kanka's face.
Blood runs from Yudhishthira's nose, and Sairandhri catches the drops in a vessel before they reach the floor.

Brihannala is kept outside, because Arjuna has sworn that whoever draws his brother's blood outside battle will not live. The year began with dice, and it ends with dice, and the hidden king bleeding, still silent.
Then the brothers walk in wearing royal clothes, take the royal seats, and Arjuna tells Virata who they are. The king offers his daughter, Princess Uttara, to Arjuna. And Arjuna says no.
I was her teacher, he says, and she trusted me as a daughter trusts a father. Let her marry my son, Abhimanyu. Here's the teaching.
In the Taittiriya Upanishad, a teacher sends students out into life with these words: let your mother be a god to you, your father, your teacher, your guest.
Acharya devo bhava: treat the teacher as divine. It's why Hindu students touch a teacher's feet, and why Guru Purnima is a day to honor teachers.
Many teachers read Arjuna's answer as the other side of it: a teacher guards that trust. Today, think of the coaches, tutors and mentors who've held yours. In Hindu teaching, that bond is sacred.

how: The Virata book closes with the Pandavas revealed and the marriage of Princess Uttara to Abhimanyu, and retellings pause on Arjuna's refusal to marry the student he taught.

o: the prince who drives Arjuna's chariot to battle
the Matsya king who learns who his guests really are
the Kuru elder who leads the cattle raid

games.q: the year ends — tap the pairs.
p: gathered the Kurus' cloths for the dolls
caught the blood in a vessel

s: 'acharya devo bhava' means treat the teacher as divine
it comes from the Taittiriya Upanishad's words to students, and families still teach it.
he said she was like a daughter to him, and she married his son Abhimanyu.
Brihannala was kept outside while Kanka bled
Arjuna had sworn that whoever drew his brother's blood outside of battle would not live.

games.q: you're Arjuna. the king you served all year offers you his daughter, the princess you taught to dance. what do you say?
o: say she trusted you as a daughter, and offer your son Abhimanyu instead.
games.why: Arjuna says no for her sake: a teacher she trusted like a father should not become her husband. she marries Abhimanyu.

practice: Bring to mind a teacher who mattered to you: at school, at a temple, a coach, a grandparent who taught you a prayer. Many Hindus bow to a teacher, or touch their feet, to say what words can't.
Sit tall, bring your palms together at your heart, and breathing in, see their face; breathing out, give your thanks. If you pray, you can hold them in your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Virata. The king who struck his own dice partner, and learned soon after that he had been hosting the Pandavas all year.

orig.note: 'living unknown': the name for the Pandavas' year in disguise. in Hindi the jñ sounds like 'gy'.

carryVoice: Your line: acharya devo bhava: the teacher's trust is sacred. The masks are set down. That's the Virata story, done.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Virata Parva (Go-harana and Vaivahika), Arjuna's battle with the Kurus, the dice thrown at Kanka, the Pandavas revealed, and the marriage of Uttara and Abhimanyu
Taittiriya Upanishad 1.11: the teacher's parting instruction (matri devo bhava, pitri devo bhava, acharya devo bhava, atithi devo bhava)
